headline: Flow-matching and language models steer generative design of proteins and peptides
label: Generative Protein Design Models
summary: Bioinformatics papers dated 2026-08-01 apply flow matching, language-model steering, and reward design to protein and peptide generation.
synthesis: The dominant thread is generative modeling conditioned on design objectives. PI-Mamba pairs flow matching with a Mamba state-space architecture to generate protein backbones with exact local covalent geometry at linear-time inference. TiDE-Ab applies SE(3) flow matching with time-dependent classifier-free guidance to epitope-specific antibody design, and PepGen conditions a protein language model on allele, partial motifs, and affinity to generate MHC-II binding peptides. PROSOUNDS steers protein language model activations using surrogate-model uncertainty, while the TCR generation study addresses Goodhart-driven reward hacking during RL fine-tuning through plug-and-play reward designs. PreFold-dG extends this toward evaluation by predicting binding ΔG from Boltz-2 intermediate embeddings. The remaining items are heterogeneous, spanning VAE curriculum learning on MSAs, circular alignment for cyclic peptide motifs, and transfer-entropy contact words for allostery. The shared advance is explicit conditioning or steering of generative models toward specified design objectives.
